# Persistence Dynamics

> A theory of what makes things last. Two operations (hold, cross), each active or latent, give four regimes (Potentiality, Construction, Encounter, Conservation) in one forced order. The unit is the persistor, a holon in Koestler's sense: one cycle that creates the structure for the next. Every closed cycle is one part of a larger one.

- [The persistor](https://persistencedynamics.com/persistor/): the unit of the theory; everything that persists is a persistor
- [The theory](https://persistencedynamics.com/theory/): how a persistor works, in eight steps, and how it could be wrong
- [What came before](https://persistencedynamics.com/lineage/): the traditions the theory builds on
- [About](https://persistencedynamics.com/about/): Raimo van der Klein, Encounter, and the paper (Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.20415561)
